author: sjm41
body:
* **PTHR ID & PTN node:**
PTN001899725

DIHYDROLIPOAMIDE ACETYLTRANSFERASE COMPONENT OF PYRUVATE DEHYDROGENASE COMPLEX (PTHR43178)

* **Sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):**
Dmel Dbct (FlyBase=FBgn0030612|UniProtKB=Q9VXY3)
Human DBT (UniProtKB=P11182)
etc


* **Type of Issue: Erroneous source or erroneous propagation, or other issue**
Both?

Fly Dbct (human ortholog = DBT) is the transferase component of the **branched-chain alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase complex** and has the activity of GO:0043754/EC:2.3.1.168 (dihydrolipoyllysine-residue (2-methylpropanoyl)transferase activity).

Both these genes are the sole fly/human members of PTHR43178.

So there seems to be a a few problems here:

1. PTHR43178 is called DIHYDROLIPOAMIDE ACETYLTRANSFERASE COMPONENT OF **PYRUVATE DEHYDROGENASE COMPLEX** - i.e. it refers a different (albeit related) complex.

2. PTHR43178 is annotated with [**acetyl**transferase activity](http://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO%3A0016407), which is consistent with the Panther name, but not the function of the human/fly members. That annotation is based on two sources:

(ARATH|TAIR=locus=2083358|UniProtKB=Q9M7Z1)
- this is Arabidopsis BCE2 (Lipoamide acyltransferase component of **branched-chain alpha-keto acid dehydrogenase complex**, mitochondrial)
- UP annotates it to EC:2.3.1.168 (=GO:0043754), which is correct
- But it has an EXP GO annotation to **acetyl**transferase activity, which is wrong - should be **acyl**transferase activity, or probably the much more specific GO:0043754

(ECOLI|EnsemblGenome=BAB96685|UniProtKB=P06959)
- this is aceF (Dihydrolipoyllysine-residue acetyltransferase component of **pyruvate dehydrogenase complex**)
- UP annotates it to EC:2.3.1.12 (= GO:0004742), which is correct
- and it has an EXP GO annotation to GO:0004742 (dihydrolipoyllysine-residue **acetyl**transferase activity), also correct


Bottom lines:
-  PTN001899725/PTHR43178 needs splitting/revising to correct the name/members/GO-MF annotation
-  the TAIR annotation to BCE2 needs checking/revising  @tberardini
title: PTN001899725 (PTHR43178)

author: tberardini
body: TAIR annotation reviewed and updated. Thank you @sjm41 for pointing out the error and the assistance with resolving it.

author: marcfeuermann
body:
**This one indeed required some more work. Thanks for filling my boring days ;-)
I decided to delete all PAINT annotations and re-annotate following all your points. Fortunately, we did not use many primary annotations for PAINTing**

Fly Dbct (human ortholog = DBT) is the transferase component of the branched-chain alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase complex and has the activity of GO:0043754/EC:2.3.1.168 (dihydrolipoyllysine-residue (2-methylpropanoyl)transferase activity).
Both these genes are the sole fly/human members of PTHR43178.
So there seems to be a a few problems here:
    PTHR43178 is called DIHYDROLIPOAMIDE ACETYLTRANSFERASE COMPONENT OF PYRUVATE DEHYDROGENASE COMPLEX - i.e. it refers a different (albeit related) complex.

**I renamed the family as:
BRANCHED CHAIN ALPHA_KETOACID DEHYDROGENASE COMPLEX
This correponds to the main node of the family.
I also associated the corresponding CC to the corresponding node**

"PTHR43178 is annotated with [acetyltransferase activity](http://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO%3A0016407), which is consistent with the Panther name, but not the function of the human/fly members. That annotation is based on two sources:
(ARATH|TAIR=locus=2083358|UniProtKB=Q9M7Z1)
this is Arabidopsis BCE2 (Lipoamide acyltransferase component of branched-chain alpha-keto acid dehydrogenase complex, mitochondrial)

UP annotates it to EC:2.3.1.168 (=GO:0043754), which is correct
 But it has an EXP GO annotation to acetyltransferase activity, which is wrong - should be acyltransferase activity, or probably the much more specific GO:0043754

**None of the correct Go terms is available as a primary annotation for PAINTing.  
We have Contibutes_to "branched-chain alpha-keto acid dehydrogenase activity". Is this correct ?
I f yes I could add this one, if not, I leave the MF part blank for the moment (for DBT node).**

(ECOLI|EnsemblGenome=BAB96685|UniProtKB=P06959)
    this is aceF (Dihydrolipoyllysine-residue acetyltransferase component of pyruvate dehydrogenase complex)
    UP annotates it to EC:2.3.1.12 (= GO:0004742), which is correct
    and it has an EXP GO annotation to GO:0004742 (dihydrolipoyllysine-residue acetyltransferase activity), also correct

**This node keeps the "dihydrolipoyllysine-residue acetyltransferase activity (GO:0004742)" annotation as well as "pyruvate dehydrogenase complex (GO:0045254) 
The node results from a duplication within bacteria. Not sure we can split it from the family but we can easily distinguish it in the evolutionary model.**

Bottom lines:

    PTN001899725/PTHR43178 needs splitting/revising to correct the name/members/GO-MF annotation
    the TAIR annotation to BCE2 needs checking/revising @tberardini

**Thanks a lot for clearing the situation here. And thanks @tberardini for the update of the Arabisopsis annotation.
Marc**

author: sjm41
body:
> I renamed the family as:
BRANCHED CHAIN ALPHA_KETOACID DEHYDROGENASE COMPLEX

I think that's too broad a name since the complex has 3 distinct enzymatic components from different families. We could follow UniProt's lead here (https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P11182/entry) and go with:
"Lipoamide acyltransferase component of BRANCHED CHAIN ALPHA_KETOACID DEHYDROGENASE COMPLEX"


> None of the correct Go terms is available as a primary annotation for PAINTing.
We have Contibutes_to "branched-chain alpha-keto acid dehydrogenase activity". Is this correct ?
I f yes I could add this one, if not, I leave the MF part blank for the moment (for DBT node).

That's a shame.  I'll take a look for some EXP when I get chance.
I'd avoid adding  Contibutes_to "branched-chain alpha-keto acid dehydrogenase activity" since that represents the overall effect of the 3 separable reactions of the 3 distinct components in the complex, and the MF term is probably going to obsoleted - see https://github.com/geneontology/go-ontology/issues/29951

author: marcfeuermann
body: Thanks for your answer, it makes sense and I will follow your suggestions.
